headline: Three children and a teacher shot dead in Oregon
summary: A 16-year-old shot at the locked doors of Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, just before 1pm Thursday until he was inside. He killed three children, aged five, eight and 11, and a teacher. A bystander followed him in and shot him dead; police arrived three minutes later. A seven-year-old and a teacher are in critical condition.

cover_question.q: Why didn't the locked doors work?

cover_answer: He shot the locks until he was in. A bystander stopped him.
table_question: A stranger ran in to stop it. Would you want that to be the plan?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A teenager with a gun got into a school in Oregon, a long way from here, and hurt people. Three children and a teacher died. A grown-up nearby ran in and stopped him, and the police came three minutes later, about as long as brushing your teeth twice. Your school has locked doors and grown-ups whose job is keeping you safe, and they have it.
5-7.why: Only if they hear it. One helper, three minutes, then their own school.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event and reads your face first, so the script leaves out the children's ages and gives them the helper who ran in and the three minutes, measured in toothbrushing. Expect "could it happen at my school?" Very rarely, and your school practises for it.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: A 16-year-old shot at the locked doors of an elementary school in Bend, Oregon on Thursday until he got in. He killed three children and a teacher. A man outside followed him in and shot him; police arrived three minutes later. The school went into lockdown, the drill yours practises.
8-12.why: Doors, lockdown, the helper, the police. The drill is the mechanism.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script runs one chain: he shot the doors, got in, a man followed, police came three minutes later. The lockdown drill is the mechanism they know from their own school, and the watches say what the kids inside did. Expect "why did he do it?" Police haven't said, and haven't named him.

13-17.script: Should a bystander with a gun be the plan? A 16-year-old shot his way into a Bend, Oregon elementary school and killed three children and a teacher. A bystander followed him in and shot him dead; police came three minutes later. Second: at least 140 school shootings this year. What moves that number?
13-17.why: A bystander as the plan, and 140 this year. Hold both.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a stranger with a gun ended it in minutes, and a plan that depends on one is not a plan. The script asks that first, then hands them the count, at least 140 this year, and asks what moves it. Expect "why does this keep happening here?" Say you don't know, then argue it with them.

5-7.q: Could it happen at my school?
5-7.a: It is very rare. Your school has locked doors and practises what to do, and the grown-ups there have it.

8-12.q: Why didn't the locked doors work?
8-12.a: They were locked. He shot at them until he was through.
A local 16-year-old. Police haven't named him or said why.

13-17.q: Was the man who shot him a hero?
13-17.a: The governor called it heroic, and a heavy burden. Both true.
235 last year, at least 140 this year, one database counts.
